claims.statement: The official TED Search API provides unauthenticated access to published procurement notices for analysis and reuse, including structured sector and location classifications.
Poland's e-Zamówienia platform exposes APIs for domestic notices, statistics, procurement plans, and related procurement data; reading BZP notices does not require the full integration procedure.
Hypothesis: small energy contractors will pay for bid/no-bid decisions and reusable evidence rather than another broad tender alert, especially if the product measures won margin and staff time.

contrary_evidence: Notice data is open and reusable, so public-search and alert features alone have little moat.
Existing procurement platforms already offer filters and subscriptions; differentiation depends on vertical workflow and private outcomes.

economics.acquisition_route: Free high-precision digest, installer-wholesaler partnerships, association distribution, and proof of hours saved in a family-company pilot
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 600 customers at 9,000 PLN average ARR plus selective services creates over 5m PLN revenue; a profitable majority-owned data workflow could support over 5m PLN founder equity in four to seven years
economics.founder_time: 10-15 hours weekly for a single energy vertical; analyst-assisted services must be capped or delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Alert and workspace software can exceed 85% gross margin; assisted bid packs may yield 45-65%, producing 65-80% blended margin
economics.payback: One avoided unsuitable bid or one additional profitable award can repay a year; target vendor CAC payback within six months
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 700-2,500 PLN monthly per contractor plus 1,500-6,000 PLN for analyst-assisted bid packs
economics.retention_or_repeat: Tender calendars repeat and the evidence vault becomes more valuable; retention weakens if a contractor bids only occasionally

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A private graph of requirement patterns, bid decisions, pricing assumptions, clarifications, competitors, awards, and realised margin
fingerprint.customer: Small Polish renewable, retrofit, electrical, and energy-audit contractors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Free local tender digest, family-business proof case, wholesaler and accountant referrals, and industry association channels
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Vertical tender feed, qualification extraction, bid/no-bid scoring, reusable evidence vault, and outcome analytics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Contractor pays a monthly workspace subscription and optional fixed fee for a structured bid pack
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A relevant tender or procurement plan appears and the contractor must quickly decide whether and how to bid

founder_fit: The family renewable business can lawfully test relevance, bid triage, and time savings. The founder's data and AI strengths suit document parsing and outcome modelling, while distribution can be product-led and through wholesalers rather than high-energy networking.
risks: Automated eligibility interpretation can miss a mandatory condition and waste bid effort.
Low tender frequency could cause weak retention in the initial niche.
Sensitive bid data requires strict tenant isolation and must never facilitate collusion.

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical procurement intelligence and bid-workflow SaaS
structure.control_point: The contractor's accumulated bid/no-bid and evidence memory at the moment resources are committed
structure.critical_dependency: Customers contributing truthful bid outcomes and the vertical having sufficient tender frequency

thesis: Build a vertical tender intelligence and bid-memory workspace for renewable installers, energy auditors, and retrofit contractors. It detects relevant Polish and EU notices, parses technical eligibility and bill-of-quantity clues, and learns from each user's bid/no-bid, pricing, clarification, and award result. Public alerts are the wedge; the private outcome graph and reusable evidence library become the control point.
title: Energy Tender Bid Memory for Small Contractors
uncertainties: How often small energy contractors bid and what they currently spend on preparation.
Whether award data and tender attachments are consistent enough for reliable margin features.
Whether contractors will enter sensitive bid prices and outcomes into a third-party system.
